QM is a reversal pattern if used in the right locations.

The best place (as always) to really assess it's potential is to look at your charts. You'll learn more by looking at your charts than you will any book or forum - get the basics from here and then go and spend hours pouring over your charts until spotting QM's etc and where / how to trade them are part of your subconscious.

In terms of the 'why' they work, let's take a short QM setup...

1. When it forms the 2nd high this is where the professional money is shorting - this is also where novice sellers / weak hands have placed there stops and breakout / trend traders have placed long orders.

2. Price making the 2nd low is in affect the tip off that a reversal is coming - a seasoned trader spots this and is looking to short. If this new low also happens to trigger a break of a significant level / TL then all the better - the more noticeable the location the more likely clever traders are looking to enter the market with shorts.

Of course the new low also trips some stops and encourages novice shorts on board who look to bail out as price retraces - breakout traders are weak players who don't hold for long - this helps the 'distribution' process and allows the Pro's to load up shorts on the retrace to form the RS - you should be able to predict where this RS 'should' form.

3. The process is complete - Pro traders are fully loaded on shorts, weak hands have been had their orders utilised for liquidity and now the reversal can play out.

No access to charts right now but look over a chart and think about who is participating and why at each 'leg' and what their orders are doing to price and it should become clear...have a go at annotating a chart and I'll review over the weekend when I get some time.

But this oneI would consider a proper QM. It is proportioned. It makes a HH, but then a LL that shows the trend is changing. It has not a HH or LL that gets over a lot of previous H or L.

In the chart we are discussing, although, there is what I would consider a proper QM, as I signal the yellow HH, that just gets over the previous H, showing bull intentions. Then price came back to demand, and then shoots up.

So one of the interpretations we could do of a QM is that price is taking out orders on both sides with the HH and LL. Why? Because over the Highs and Lows there use to be clusters of orders. As breakout trading and SL over the Highs and Lows is one of the most extended ways of trading ("if resistance is broken, then buy, and put SL under the last low"), there use to be a lot of orders. This order positions are well known, so when price goes over a H or L they trigger a lot of orders. But what happen if price inmediately goes the other way? panic and SL triggering that add fuel to the movement. In this charts, a lot of sellers were trapped on the LL, that became buyers when their SL were triggered, adding fuel to the bull movement. At the same time the retail uninformed sellers were being the counterpart of the big money buyers, that need a lot of sellers to fulfill their orders. On this chart we could read that then price arrives to a Supply level, doing a HH. There were yet sell orders, so price came back to the next demand where the QM completed. When price did the HH it shows the bull strength, and consumed the few Sell orders that were left on the level. So the level was cleaned, and the sellers that were trapped on the LL that started triggering their SL, the way to the highs was ready, and as it happens, it shoots up.

1. Aware traders see the oncoming HTF supply, the ITs know this, so just before the HTF supply they turn price creating a nice area to be faked for later on, confusing a lot of traders who were long and using the HTF supply as their targets, this would cause a lot of traders to panic and exit their longs early and cause a drop in price assisting the ITs with their intentions, which is to create a low which can be faked later on.

2. The ITs have joined in selling with the retail, this would entice traders who were aware of the HTF supply to go short now, thinking that price has turned before the supply creating panic and fear of missing the move AKA: trigger-happy sellers. The ITs know this, and know there are millions of buy stops to be had, to assist them in reaching HTF supply.

3. This is where it gets fun! Notice the high above (Marked with a line), there will no doubt be a lot of sellers there attempting to fade the high with their stops just above, this gives the ITs and incentive to smash this level and take the LQ for the push up in to supply, this attracts BO buyers, and on this account they would have been ok, if they were not greedy, however not the brightest move buying into supply, but they would have been ok in this case for a little while, and are currently enjoying the free ride up.

Putting them aside for one moment; we are now in HTF supply, and who waits at HTF supply??? Sellers and lots of them. The ITs know this and where are we taught to put our stops?? Just outside of the zone, the ITs know this, and in this case they engulf the zone collecting all of those buy stops to sell into. But hold on, engulfed the zone, should price not go higher??? Yes it should, if it was an engulf, more than likely there was a supply just above this zone that the ITs used to FO into, a clever move created by the ITs on unsuspecting traders.

4. With all the buy stops for the ITs to sell into, they have enough LQ to drop this baby!! And this is exactly what they do. This will create panic for the BO buyers from earlier and encourage them to sell adding fuel to the move, also this will attract sellers that were short at supply originally to short again, what do we call this?? Oh yes, CHASING PRICE, NOT A RECOMMENDED PRACTICE. We have now arrived at an S/R flip area, and as most of us know, these areas attract traders attempting to fade the area even though we’ve just come out of supply, BO sellers in the anticipation price will break the support level. What price does in this instance is collect more LQ, faking up and down, collecting more LQ from all these small FOs for the push down, this forms a nice supply zone, lining neatly with our QM level. Think about this for a moment, these levels attract BO sellers, and also traders who are attempting to fade, with all these short up and down moves (price Faking out) this would have triggered in most of the BO sellers and stopped them out collecting their buy stops, also doing the same for the traders trying to fade the level, triggering them in and stopping them out. A nice way to get short would you not agree?

5. The ITs have pushed price down, and pushed it hard, this again will attract more BO selling, but don’t forget the LTF traders getting stopped out who are going long at minor demand zones, this all adds to the ITs LQ. We now have reached the low (2) Do we see a break of this level and a continuation or do we see a FO, we wait for the ITs to make their move. They FO the area this stops a load of traders who were fading the low again giving sell stops for the ITs to buy into, and this would be our Lower low of the QM formation. With all this LQ and remembering the BO sellers will begin panicking once they see price reverse and will begin thinking of closing their position i.e. buying. This will cause confusion among traders, and encourage revenge trade after revenge trade taking loss after loss, filling the accounts of the big cats as they’re smiling all the way to the bank.

6. The ITs work is done, once price reaches the supply created by them, and confused enough traders, and making sure they are the only, or should I say the main traders short, they enjoy a nice drop to their target.

This is definitely not the only way of looking at a QM formation and I am sure there are many more experienced traders who could paint a clearer view, however this is how I see it for now, and it is definitely working to my advantage in testing.

This is how I understand QMs

They appear at the end of a bullish or bearish trends, so it's a reversal trade set up.

Price action needs these things to happen for Bearish QMs: 1. Pre-existing up trend with HLs + HHs 2. Price makes HH into HTF Supply 3. Price makes a bearish engulf or a newly formed RBD/DBD inside HTF Supply 4. Price drops breaking most recent demand, support, or previous low. Makes LL 5. Price then rallies up to the origin of the bearish engulf or the newly formed RBD/DBD inside the HTF Supply 6. Price is then expected to significantly drop into a new downtrend. Money

Here's for the Bullish QMs: 1. Pre-existing down trend with LHs + LLs 2. Price makes LL into HTF Demand 3. Price makes a bullish engulf or a newly formed DBR/RBR inside HTF Demand 4. Price rallies breaking most recent supply, resistance, or previous high. Makes HH 5. Price then drops down to the origin of the bullish engulf or the newly formed DBR/RBR inside the HTF Demand 6. Price is then expected to significantly rally into a new uptrend. Money
